Customer deposits surged to roughly $750 million from about $145 million at the start of the year, signaling strong demand for Bloom’s capacity. He swapped out $SNDK, viewing energy as a more structural long-term trade than memory, and increased allocations to $INTC, $NBIS, $CRDO, and $LITE which are down significantly. text:
$BE under $200? This market is full of pansies!

Just added $BE at $190/share in my ultra concentrated Asymmetric Bets portfolio as a 16% position.

What's interesting is I already made 186% on this stock earlier this year. You can look and see I added the stock at $90 in December and sold it for a 186% gain at $274/share on June 1.

Many remember my YouTube video where I explained the thesis and origin story of the company before this became a consensus energy winner.

Now I'm back in, especially after another record setting earnings. What stood out most to me was customer deposits surging to roughly $750 million from about $145 million at the start of the year, a clear sign customers are paying upfront to lock in Bloom’s capacity before it’s even built.

New positions often require sacrifices though. So I chose to swap out $SNDK in the portfolio. The rationale is simple. I see energy as being a more structural trade than memory. $BE is a stock I can hold for 10 years while $SNDK and memory has an uphill battle to prove to investors it has long term durability. 

I also used cash to bump up my allocations on $INTC, $NBIS, $CRDO, and $LITE. All are down huge in the last two weeks.

This portfolio is up over 50% all time despite being down 20% in the past month because I was early to AI infrastructure stocks before the herd. 

Tough drawdown, but have to stay focused on the best companies in this buildout.

text:
Investors are betting on more upside in US Treasuries.

The extra cost investors are willing to pay for call options on longer-dated Treasuries relative to puts is up to ~50 basis points, the highest since March 2025.

This marks a sharp reversal from a 250-basis-point premium for puts over calls in late September.

This suggests investors are increasingly betting on further gains in Treasury prices.

Furthermore, one options trade is targeting a drop in the 10Y Note Yield to ~4.60% within a month, involving ~65,000 contracts and costing ~$7 million in premium.

This comes as the 10Y Note Yield has declined below 5.00% for the first time since September 23rd, now down -40 basis points from the October 7th peak.

The bond market is seeing massive swings in price and sentiment.

The catch? HBM shortages and customer financing could limit how quickly this opportunity translates into cash flow.

text:
NHTSA announced today that they are proposing new rules aimed at removing U.S. federal regulatory barriers for autonomous vehicles without steering wheels or pedals, such as @Tesla's Cybercab.

The proposed changes include:
• Eliminating requirements for manually operated turn signal controls in vehicles without steering wheels or pedals: "NHTSA has concluded that the self-canceling and manually operated control requirements in the current standard are unnecessary for turn signal operating units that are installed on vehicles without manually operated driving controls."

• Allowing autonomous driving systems to control turn signals, hazard lights, and high/low beams without traditional driver-operated switches.

• Removing certain dashboard indicator requirements for turn signals and high beams in vehicles without manual driving controls.

• Allowing optional cyan-colored exterior lights to indicate when a vehicle is operating autonomously, with standardized requirements for their placement, brightness, and operation.

• Eliminating outdated restrictions on vertical headlight arrangements, giving automakers greater design flexibility.

• Allowing modern integrated headlights to be tested at manufacturer-specified voltages rather than requiring 12.8 volts.

NHTSA says the changes are intended to eliminate unnecessary regulatory barriers, reduce costs, and enable innovation without compromising vehicle safety.

text:
$CRDO getting hit pretty hard today following $MXL’s plans to enter the 1.6T AEC market.

Competition isn’t anything new here. $ALAB and several others have already been making moves into the space, and given how attractive the market is, more competition was inevitable.

Credo still has an estimated 90%+ share of the AEC market and relationships with 5/6 major hyperscalers. 

$MXL isn’t expecting initial revenues until 2027, with a more meaningful ramp in 2028.

Definitely something to monitor, but I think the market is overreacting here. $CRDO is starting to look ridiculously cheap.

- October 22 marked the 1st time since the COVID crash that long/short, systematic, and multi-strategy hedge funds tracked by Goldman Sachs ALL lost more than 1% in a single day.

- Tech-focused hedge funds: down ~10% in October

- Asia-focused hedge funds: down ~9% in October

Quite the divergence, I do think there’s been a ton of irrational selling now, hedge fund deleveraging seems to be a major contributor.

This week @elonmusk challenged the industry and @bscholl @boomsupersonic delivered.   

On Tuesday’s $SPCX earnings call, Elon talked about how to quicken the pace to get power up and running:   “Casting is the real bottleneck. And if anything, it seems to be getting worse. So that means that SpaceX can bring power on line 12 to 18 months faster than anyone else. That's the kind of advantage that's difficult to replicate unless someone else is doing advanced casting".

Today, Boom announced the world's first all-digital foundry to cast single crystal turbine blades and vanes.   

Congrats to Blake and the Boom team on the huge milestone. We’re thrilled to be investors in both @boomsupersonic and @SpaceX, solving AI’s biggest bottleneck and reindustrializing America.
